metadata.description: Natural gas & LNG import terminals, major transmission pipelines, and strategic underground storage facilities in Germany.
primary_sources: FNB Gas (Association of German Transmission System Operators)

properties.name: FSRU Wilhelmshaven (LNG terminal Höegh Esperanza)
properties.capacity: approx. 5–7.5 bn m³ of gas / year
properties.summary: Germany’s first floating import terminal for liquefied natural gas (LNG).
properties.description: Built in just 10 months in 2022. Turns cryogenic liquefied gas (−162 °C) from tankers back into its gaseous state and feeds it directly into the transmission grid.
consumer_products: Industrial gas for chemicals and glass

aha_moment.title: Warmth for millions of living rooms
aha_moment.explanation: A single LNG tanker delivers enough energy to reliably heat around 50,000 single-family homes for a whole year.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Keeps showers hot and radiators working on cold winter days in the north and west.

properties.name: LNG Terminal Brunsbüttel (Elbe port)
properties.capacity: approx. 4–5 bn m³ of gas / year
properties.summary: Key LNG terminal at the mouth of the Elbe for industry and northern Germany.
properties.description: Floating terminal where the Elbe and the Kiel Canal meet. Directly supplies the energy-intensive basic materials industry in the ChemCoast Park Brunsbüttel and the area around Hamburg.

aha_moment.title: No gas, no bread on the table
aha_moment.explanation: Natural gas is not only a heating fuel but an essential raw material for producing ammonia and mineral fertiliser. Without gas, crop yields drop drastically.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Through the fertiliser market, Brunsbüttel’s chemical plants help secure the food supply of all of Central Europe.

properties.name: Dornum gas landing station (Europipe)
properties.capacity: approx. 18 bn m³ of gas / year
properties.summary: Main entry point for Norwegian pipeline gas into Germany.
properties.description: This is where the huge Europipe subsea pipeline from the Norwegian offshore gas fields Troll and Ekofisk comes ashore. Norway is now Germany’s most important gas supplier.
consumer_products: Grid gas for southern and western Germany

aha_moment.title: Norway’s offshore power on the beach
aha_moment.explanation: Around a third of Germany’s entire gas demand arrives invisibly across the seabed from Norway, landing right here on the East Frisian coast.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: The most reliable pillar of Germany’s modern energy supply.

properties.name: Rehden Gas Storage (Lower Saxony)
properties.capacity: approx. 4 bn m³ of working gas (largest storage facility in Western Europe)
properties.description: A gigantic underground porous-rock storage facility 2,000 metres deep. Its capacity is enough to supply around two million households through an entire cold winter.
consumer_products: Pressure balancing in the national grid

aha_moment.title: Germany’s energy store 2 km underground
aha_moment.explanation: In porous sandstone layers that held natural gas millions of years ago, gas is now stored in summer to cushion peaks in demand in freezing January.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Prevents supply shortages during extreme cold spells.

properties.name: Waidhaus Compressor Station (Upper Palatinate)
properties.capacity: Hub for approx. 25 bn m³ / year
properties.summary: Central continental gas crossing point on the German-Czech border.
properties.description: Historically an entry point for Russian gas, now converted to reverse flow: gas can be moved flexibly between Germany, Czechia, Austria and south-eastern Europe.

aha_moment.title: Compressing and pumping over hundreds of kilometres
aha_moment.explanation: Gas loses pressure through friction as it flows. Huge turbines in Waidhaus recompress it to up to 100 bar so that it keeps flowing all the way to Munich or Stuttgart.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Keeps Bavaria’s glass and ceramics industry and car factories running.

properties.name: NETRA gas transmission pipeline (Dornum – Salzwedel)
properties.summary: Main east-west supply axis for Norwegian gas across northern Germany.
properties.description: Connects the Dornum coastal landing station with storage facilities and the eastern German gas grid.
consumer_products: Supply for northern and eastern Germany

aha_moment.title: An invisible high-pressure motorway
aha_moment.explanation: A single underground steel pipe 1.2 metres wide carries more energy than dozens of high-voltage power lines combined.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Supplies millions of households with reliable heating energy.

properties.name: EUGAL Pipeline (European Gas Link)
properties.flow_direction: Baltic Sea / Lubmin → Brandenburg → Saxony → Czechia
properties.summary: The most powerful twin-line gas route in Central Europe.
properties.description: Runs dead straight south from the Baltic coast to the Czech border. It is to be converted for hydrogen transport as part of the European hydrogen core network.
consumer_products: Transit gas for south-eastern Europe & eastern Germany

aha_moment.title: Ready for green hydrogen
aha_moment.explanation: Germany’s most modern gas route was built hydrogen-ready and will form the bridge to a carbon-neutral future.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Backbone of industry’s future clean energy supply.

properties.name: MEGAL Pipeline (Central European Gas Pipeline)
properties.summary: The great southern German gas transversal across Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg.
properties.description: Connects southern Germany with the western European transmission networks and secures the energy supply of southern Germany’s automotive, engineering and chemical clusters.
consumer_products: District heating for Munich and Nuremberg

aha_moment.title: The lifeline of southern German industry
aha_moment.explanation: From BMW and Audi to glassmaking in the Bavarian Forest: without the constant pressure of the MEGAL, production lines would stand still.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Keeps hundreds of thousands of industrial jobs in southern Germany productive.

source.name: Open Grid Europe MEGAL data sheet

properties.name: Salzwedel Gas Hub (NETRA end point)
properties.capacity: Important distribution hub for northern Germany
properties.summary: Eastern end and transfer point of the NETRA gas transmission pipeline.
properties.description: At the Salzwedel station, natural gas from the NETRA is handed over to the onward German transmission network. The hub links northern German landing points with centres of consumption and storage facilities.

aha_moment.title: From North Sea gas into the grid
aha_moment.explanation: Gas landing in Dornum or Wilhelmshaven flows through the NETRA to Salzwedel and is distributed from here across the whole German grid.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Part of the natural gas that reaches homes and power plants in northern Germany passes through this hub.

properties.name: EUGAL southern transfer point (German-Czech border)
properties.capacity: High-pressure transfer towards Czechia / southern Germany
properties.summary: Southern end and transfer point of the EUGAL pipeline.
properties.description: The EUGAL carries natural gas south from the Baltic coast. At this hub, gas is handed over towards the Czech grid and southern German centres of consumption.

aha_moment.title: A gas motorway to the south
aha_moment.explanation: EUGAL is one of Germany’s largest gas transmission pipelines, linking the Baltic landing point with the south and neighbouring countries.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Gas from this route can end up in German homes as well as in neighbouring countries.

properties.name: MEGAL western transfer point (towards France)
properties.summary: Western end and transfer point of the MEGAL pipeline.
properties.description: The MEGAL (Central European Gas Pipeline) is one of the central east-west axes of the German transmission network. At this hub, gas is handed over towards France and the south-west.

aha_moment.title: An east-west gas bridge
aha_moment.explanation: Through the MEGAL, gas flows right across southern Germany – from the Czech border to the French border.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Many gas deliveries in southern and western Germany and to neighbouring countries use this route.

properties.name: Lubmin / Greifswald landing station (EUGAL start)
properties.summary: Northern starting point of the EUGAL on the Baltic coast.
properties.description: Near Lubmin / Greifswald, natural gas from Baltic Sea connections is brought ashore and fed into the EUGAL. The site is one of the central import and distribution hubs in the north-east.

aha_moment.title: Baltic gateway for natural gas
aha_moment.explanation: This is where gas from the Baltic Sea arrives and begins its journey south through the German transmission network.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Part of the gas that reaches eastern and southern Germany starts its journey here.
